The same tree a `CTMLScreen` would open, drawn over the game instead of in front of it. Nothing about the tree says which it is: the same ctml root, the same elements, the same styles and the same interpreter behind all of it. Whichever of the two the host builds is the answer.

So this is that screen with everything the user could do to it taken out. A hud gets no press, no wheel, no key and no cursor, which means:

- callbacks never fire, so a callback property on a hud element says nothing;
- hover:, focus:, focus-visible:, focus-within: and active: never hold, there being nothing to tell the tree about the mouse or the keyboard;
- a draggable box is never dragged, and a scrollbar is drawn but cannot be taken hold of.

Everything a script drives still works: the variables a ${name} reads, a class list written by hand, and scroll-x, scroll-y and scroll-into, which a hud animates the way a screen does.

A `DOMContext` is still what the tree is shown through, since that is where the variables live. It just never has `DOMContext.fire` called on it from here.

```java
import net.tutla.craftytml.client.render.CTMLHud;
```
